newsitem.title: UK: Digital radio sets seen on UK market by early 98.
newsitem.headline: Digital radio sets seen on UK market by early 98.

text.p: Receivers for CD-quality digital radio broadcasts are likely to go on sale in Britain from late this year or early in 1998, BBC officials said on Wednesday.

Dominic Riley, in charge of marketing the BBC's digital audio broadcasting (DAB) services, said that a number of manufacturers were expected to unveil new digital radio sets at a trade fair in Berlin in September.

He said these were likely to be put on the market in Britain around the turn of the year. The first sets are expected to be designed for in-car use but a model for the home is likely to follow shortly afterwards.
DAB has the advantages of offering CD-quality sound and a constant signal, with none of the interference from buildings in city centres and no need to retune in different regions.
Digital signals take up less of the broadcast spectrum, leaving space for supplementary services.

The BBC is pioneering DAB technology, having begun digital radio transmissions in September 1995. It is experimenting with additional services such as live coverage from several sports events and from parliament.
However, the only digital receivers currently available are prototypes which cost over 2,000 stg and are large and unwieldy.
Manufacturers are expected to try to bring the price of the new, slimmer consumer sets down well below 1,000 stg.

The BBC's DAB coverage is limited to the London area and a corridor along the motorway to Birmingham. However, it aims to fill in large areas of Britain to boost coverage to around 60 percent of the country by spring 1998.
